project.name: RINO

project.tagline: Disagree like neighbors. Govern like the country depends on it.

principles.title: Respect without surrender
principles.summary: Strong disagreement is compatible with dignity. No person becomes an enemy merely by voting, praying, living, or reasoning differently.

principles.title: Evidence before accusation
principles.summary: Public claims should be testable, sourced, narrowly written, and correctable. Interpretation must not masquerade as fact.

principles.title: Country before faction
principles.summary: The aim is not permanent control by one camp. It is a system where major decisions require listening, negotiation, and durable consent.

principles.title: Belonging across difference
principles.summary: The working invitation is open across prior party, heritage, geography, faith, and walk of life, with equal civic standing and no demonization.

tests.name: Public Claim Integrity Check
tests.purpose: Assess whether a public-facing RINO status claim is precise, sourced, contextualized, and correctable.

criteria.name: Scope
criteria.question: Does the wording stay within what the cited record establishes?
criteria.guidance: 0 conflicts directly; 2 is materially limited or unresolved; 4 is tightly matched to the record.

criteria.name: Authority
criteria.question: Are controlling or primary sources used where available?
criteria.guidance: 0 lacks support; 2 relies on an incomplete bridge; 4 uses the most relevant primary authority.

criteria.name: Context
criteria.question: Are meaningful qualifications and contrary context preserved?
criteria.guidance: 0 omits decisive context; 2 is incomplete; 4 discloses material limitations.

criteria.name: Correction path
criteria.question: Can a reader identify review timing and request a correction?
criteria.guidance: 0 has no path; 2 has a partial path; 4 has stable review and correction mechanisms.

eboxes.title: RINO is a proposal, not yet a qualified political party
eboxes.factualSummary: This project has established a local product foundation and a protected-preview plan. It has not established or verified ballot qualification, Federal Election Commission political-party status, a registered political committee, Section 527 status, or authority to solicit contributions.
eboxes.whyItMatters: A proposed party should not borrow credibility from legal statuses it has not earned. Keeping formation, ballot access, committee registration, and tax treatment distinct protects prospective supporters and gives the project an honest roadmap.

claims.text: Federal political-party status carries criteria beyond choosing a name or launching a website.
RINO has not supplied evidence in this workspace of ballot qualification, FEC committee registration, or federal tax status.

eboxes.title: A national name does not create nationwide ballot access
eboxes.factualSummary: Federal election law defines political-party status for federal campaign-finance purposes, but states control access to their ballots. A new organization must investigate each relevant state’s current law, deadlines, petition or support rules, candidate procedures, and status-retention requirements.
eboxes.whyItMatters: A credible launch plan cannot treat one federal filing or national announcement as a substitute for state-by-state organizing. Geography, candidate strategy, timing, and legal review have to be planned together.

claims.text: Ballot access is governed by state law and varies by state.

sourceRelationships.note: States that ballot access is governed by state law and directs organizations to state election officials.
